questions.q: A particle executes simple harmonic motion between <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>–</mo><mi>A</mi><mo> </mo><mtext>and</mtext><mo> </mo><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mo>+</mo><mi>A</mi></math>. If time taken by particle to go from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>; then time taken by particle in going from <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The position of a particle performing an SHM is given by:

x=A sin(ωt+ϕ)

Since at t=0 s, the particle is at x=0, therefore the initial phase ϕ=0.

At time t=2 s, the particle is at x=A2.

∴ A2=A sin2ω⇒ω=π12 s-1

Therefore, time period

T=2πω=24 s

The total time taken from x=0 to x=A is T4=6 s.

Since the time taken from x=0 to x=A2 is 2 s, therefore the time taken from x=A2 to x=A is 4 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As can be seen from the diagram, the initial phase of the particle is given by

φ=30°= π6

The equation of motion of the particle at its initial position at time t=0 can be written as

xt=rcosθ   ...(1)

where, θ is the angular displacement of the particle at time t=t.

Since, the position of the particle at a later instant of time always lags behind its initial position at time t=0, the equation of motion of the particle at any instant of time is given by

 xt=rcosθ+φ   ...2

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (2) to obtain the required expression

x(t)=r cosωt+π6

questions.q:
Given below are two statements. One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Knowing initial position $x_0$ and initial momentum $p_0$ is enough to determine the position and momentum at any time $t$ for a simple harmonic motion with a given angular frequency $\omega$.
Reason (R): The amplitude and phase can be expressed in terms of $x_0$ and $\mathrm{p}_0$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both $(\mathbf{A})$ and $(\mathbf{R})$ are true and $(\mathbf{R})$ is the correct explanation of $(\mathbf{A})$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \text { If we express position } x(t)=A \sin (\omega t+\phi) \\ & \text { then } x_0=A \sin \phi \\ & v_0=A \omega \cos \phi \\ & \Rightarrow \tan \phi=\frac{\omega x_0}{v_0} \\ & A=\sqrt{x_0^2+\frac{v_0^2}{\omega^2}}\end{aligned}$
Hence both position and linear momentum of a particle can be expressed as a function of time if we know initial momentum and position

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The displacement equation of a particle is given by 

x=Asinωt+ϕ⇒sinωt+ϕ=xA

The velocity equation is given by,

v=ωAcosωt+ϕ⇒cosωt+ϕ=vωA

Since, sin2θ+cos2θ=1

⇒x2A2+v2ω2A2=1

The above equation represents an ellipse.

questions.q:
A light hollow cube of side length 10 cm and mass 10 g , is floating in water. It is pushed down and released to execute simple harmonic oscillations. The time period of oscillations is $y \pi \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~s}$, where the value of $y$ is
(Acceleration due to gravity, $g=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2$, density of water $=10^3 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^3$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Additional buoyant force
$\begin{aligned} & g \rho a^2 x=\sigma a^3 A \\ & A=\frac{\rho}{\sigma} \frac{g}{a} x \\ & T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\sigma a}{\rho g}} \end{aligned}$ Now, $\sigma=\frac{10 \times 10^{-3}}{10^{-3}}=10\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{10 \times 0.1}{10^3 \times 10}} \\ & =2 \pi \times 10^{-2}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The potential energy is given by 

U=mω2x22

The kinetic energy is given by K=mω2(A2-x2)2.

Using the condition that K=U,

12mω2A2-x2=12mω2x2

⇒x=A2

questions.q: A ring is hung on a nail. It can oscillate, without slipping or sliding (i) in its plane with a time period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> and (ii) back and forth in a direction perpendicular to its plane, with a period <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. The ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>T</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The time period of oscillation of physical pendulum is given by

T=2πIMgl  ...(1)

Where, I is the moment of inertia of ring about given axis and l is the distance of centre of mass of ring from the axis of rotation.

Moment of inertia of ring in its plane is given by

I1=Ic+ Md2=MR2+MR2=2MR2

Moment of inertia of ring perpendicular to its plane is given by

I2=Ic+ Md2=MR22+MR2=32MR2

Now the ratio of time period is given by 

T1T2=I1I2

⇒T1T2=2MR232MR2

⇒T1T2=43=23

questions.q: The displacement of a particle executing SHM is given by $x=10 \sin \left(w t+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) m$. The time period of motion is $3.14 \mathrm{~s}$. The velocity of the particle at $t=0$ is ______$\mathrm{m} / \mathrm{s}$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given,
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{T}=3.14=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega} \\
& \omega=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\
& \mathrm{x}=10 \sin \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\
& \mathrm{v}=\frac{\mathrm{dx}}{\mathrm{dt}}=10 \omega \cos \left(\omega \mathrm{t}+\frac{\pi}{3}\right) \\
& \text { at } \mathrm{t}=0 \\
& \mathrm{v}=10 \omega \cos \left(\frac{\pi}{3}\right)=10 \times 2 \times \frac{1}{2}[\mathrm{using} \omega=2 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}] \\
& \mathrm{v}=10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> attached to free end of a spring executes SHM with a period of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. If the mass is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> the period of oscillation increases by one second, the value of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>m</mi></math> is ________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi></math>.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Time period of oscillation is given by T=2πmk, where k is the force constant of the spring. 

∵ Spring is same, therefore, spring constant will be same.

Putting the different values,

In the first case     T=1=2πmk

In the second case  T'=2=2πm+3k

 Dividing the equations, we get

 TT'=12=mm+3

⇒mm+3=14⇒4m=m+3⇒m=1

Thus, m=1 kg

questions.q: The potential energy of a particle of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> in motion along the <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math>-axis is given by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">U</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mfenced><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>-</mo><mi>cos</mi><mn>4</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi></mrow></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi></math>. The time period of the particle for small oscillation <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><mi>sin</mi><mi>θ</mi><mo>≃</mo><mi>θ</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mfrac></mfenced><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>K</mi></math> is _____ .
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here, potential energy, U=41-cos4x J

Using the relation between conservative force and potential energy, F=-dUdx.

We have, F=-4+sin4x4=-16sin4x

For small θ, sinθ≈θ.

Acceleration of particle is a=-64xm=-64x4=-16x

As the oscillations are simple harmonic in nature, so a=-ω2x⇒ω2=16⇒ω=4 rad s-1

Now, time period of oscillation isT=2πω=π2.

Thus, the value of K=2.

questions.q: Two simple harmonic waves having equal amplitudes of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> and equal frequency of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>Hz</mi></math> are moving along the same direction. The resultant amplitude is also <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>8</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The phase difference between the individual waves is _____ degree.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If two waves have the same amplitude, frequency, and direction, but are out of phase by ϕ degrees, then the amplitude of the resultant waves is given by AR=2AcosΔϕ2

Here, A1=A2=AR=8 cm

So, cosΔϕ2=12

Or phase difference between the individual waves is Δϕ2=60°⇒Δϕ=120°.
